title: Interdependence of people
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Start from the child's own breakfast: who grew the maize, who milked the cow, who drove the lorry, who sold it. Draw the chain on the board.

skills.key_step: The child names ways people depend on each other (trade, farming, health, transport, worship) and says each side needs the other.

floor.prerequisite: Names people found in a market and what they do.
floor.question: What does a person selling sukuma wiki at the market do?

representations: a breakfast chain drawn on the board
role cards: farmer, driver, shopkeeper, nurse
string joining people who need each other
steps: Pick one thing the family uses.
Ask who made, grew, carried and sold it.
Ask what each person gets back.
contexts: milk from a dairy farmer reaching a Nairobi shop
a nurse caring for a farmer's child
a fundi building a house for a teacher

board.do: Draw a farmer and a shopkeeper with an arrow from the farmer to the shop.

board.say: What does the farmer give the shopkeeper?

board.do: Ask what the shopkeeper gives back before drawing an arrow the other way.
Write money on the return arrow.

misconceptions.ask: Can one family grow, make and do everything it needs?
misconceptions.repair: List what a family uses in one day and who made each thing.

listen_for: Only the farmer needs the shopkeeper
misconceptions.ask: A farmer sells vegetables to a shopkeeper. Who needs the other?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the shopkeeper sells if no farmers sell to him, and what the farmer does if there is no shop.

misconceptions.ask: What does a hospital give people?
misconceptions.repair: Make a matching chart of five places and what they give.

listen_for: No, money means she needs nobody
misconceptions.ask: A rich trader has lots of money. Does she depend on other people?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what she can buy if every farmer and shopkeeper stopped working.

checks.question: Give one way a farmer depends on a shopkeeper.
checks.answer: any of: sells crops to the shop, buys tools and seeds there

checks.question: Who does a sick farmer depend on?

skills.key_step: The child says what people gain when they depend on each other: goods and services they cannot make, jobs and income, use of skills, friendship.

floor.prerequisite: Names ways people depend on each other.
floor.question: Who do we depend on for medicine?

representations: a chart of benefits with pictures
the class sharing tasks for a clean-up
a story of a family that tried to do everything alone
steps: Name the people who depend on each other.
Sort the gains: goods, services, money, friendship.
Say why it is good for the county.
contexts: traders and farmers at a weekly market

board.do: Draw a ring of four people holding hands.

board.say: What would this person miss if the others left?

board.do: Write the benefit beside each person.

listen_for: Yes, strong people do things alone
misconceptions.ask: Is it bad to depend on other people?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who made the school desk, who grew the lunch and who taught the lesson.

misconceptions.ask: What do people get when they depend on each other?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a neighbour who lends a tool gives that is not money.

listen_for: No, village families do everything alone
misconceptions.ask: Do people in a village depend on each other?
misconceptions.repair: List what a village family gets from others: the posho mill, the market, the clinic, help at harvest.

misconceptions.ask: Farmers need lorries to take milk to the factory. What does this give the lorry driver?
misconceptions.repair: Act it out: the farmer pays the driver; who has money now?

checks.question: Give two benefits of people depending on each other.
checks.answer: any two of: get goods and services, jobs, income, friendship, use of skills

checks.question: A learner says needing others shows you are weak. Is this right?
checks.answer: No: everyone needs others and both sides gain
